neighborhood.distance_policy: retain a record iff its geometry (footprint polygon, or point for places) intersects the union of 1600 m geodesic buffers, i.e. ST_DWITHIN(geom, anchor_point, 1600), around every anchor that has a coordinate (>=1.5 km required); anchors without a coordinate (raw address strings, failed geocodes) cannot be buffered and are recorded only
neighborhood.containment_policy: intersection, not centroid: a footprint is kept when any part is within 1600 m of an anchor even if its centroid is farther or in another H3 cell; the H3 r7 disk (k=2 rings around each anchor cell, >=4 km reach beyond any point of the anchor cell) is only the pruning cover; bbox-overlap prefilter [-98.710152, 29.457911, -98.662565, 29.495117] precedes the exact predicate
neighborhood.possible_misses: objects whose keyed (centroid) H3 r7 cell lies outside the k-ring disk but whose geometry reaches within R of an anchor (needs a footprint > ~2.5 km across); polygons are not clipped to the buffer (whole footprint retained)
neighborhood.coverage_hole_check: COUNT(*) re-run with a k=3 disk must equal the k=2 count

gaps: Parcels excluded by case design (no county parcel file loaded).
Geocoder anchor is Census TIGER address-range interpolation (a street-segment point), not a building/parcel location.
No Overture address records for Wiseman Blvd (address layer coverage gap).

FEMA USA Structures TX vintage landed = release_dt 2025-06-06, NOT the 2023-10-03 stated in case_manifest permissible_sources (the table holds the per-state release; a discrepancy against the pre-registered vintage).

Anchor A4 (Foursquare 'Microsoft Data Center', 5150 Rogers Rd) is a place-name lookup on the owner name, included as a competing place-level anchor; it extends the neighborhood ~1.3 km beyond the geocoded point.
parcels: excluded by case design (county parcel files not loaded for DEV-1)
transport: run_query row cells are clipped (~2000 chars) and result pages are byte-budgeted; fetch_result paging (RESULT_SCAN LIMIT/OFFSET, no ORDER BY) was observed to return duplicate rows, so rows were fetched by key range as ZLIB+BASE64 of TO_JSON(ARRAY_AGG(OBJECT_CONSTRUCT_KEEP_NULL(...))) in 1500-char pieces, verified by MD5 of the base64 string and row counts per range; geometry is ST_ASWKT of the stored GEOGRAPHY (Snowflake stores ~1e-9 degree precision)

anchor_lookups.what: Foursquare lookup ADDRESS LIKE %WISEMAN% OR NAME LIKE %MICROSOFT% in r7 disk k=2 (91 rows; street places and 'Microsoft Data Center'); no place at exactly 3545 Wiseman
Overture addresses payload LIKE %Wiseman% number 3545/3535 -> 0 rows; count of any Wiseman address = 0
